clue.text: Treat with contempt a pre-exam test

definitions.meaning: a practice paper sat at school before the real examination

explanation.surface: A teacher sneers at a trial run before the real exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to deride; the noun is the British school term for a practice examination.

clue.text: Bankrupt's ultimate joke, involved in extra money being borrowed

indicators.note: involved in says the following pieces sit inside the word for extra

parts.note: extra means more

indicators.note: ultimate means the final letter of the word Bankrupt's is taken

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A bankrupt's last laugh about borrowing still more cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' places the bankrupt's final letter and the joke inside the word for extra; the definition is a home loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A home loan secured on property is the classic sum someone borrows from a lender.

clue.text: Study French city features on map

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
Tours is a city on the Loire in France

explanation.surface: Someone examines the layout of a French city on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines joining points of equal height are what a relief map shows of the land's shape.

clue.text: Initially going head first, changing to become shrewd

indicators.note: changing says the letters gathered so far are rearranged into a new order
initially points to the opening letter of the word going

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone diving in headlong and then changing course to become wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges G (the first of 'going', from 'Initially') with HEADFIRST.
explanation.definitionFit: Being far-sighted means having good judgement about the future, a close synonym for astute.

clue.text: Cordial disposition — it is evident in Jo's sister

indicators.note: is evident in says the word it shows up inside the sister's name

parts.note: Amy is one of Jo March's sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women

explanation.surface: A friendly nature is apparent in Jo March's younger sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendship and goodwill between people is exactly a cordial, peaceable disposition.

clue.text: What nave of church has, being well-kept

definitions.meaning: the nave takes its name from Latin navis, a ship, so it has the form of a vessel

explanation.surface: A church's nave, admired for being in good order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy and trim is the everyday sense; the cryptic sense is the vessel form behind the Latin word for a church's nave.

clue.text: Fail to prepare for game at Eton?

definitions.meaning: Eton College plays its own Wall Game, so players head for the wall

explanation.surface: Failing to get ready for a match at a famous school.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English public school whose Wall Game is played against a brick wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be ruined in business; literally it is setting off to the pitch for the Eton Wall Game.

clue.text: Disastrous time with student event undermined by one head of college

indicators.note: undermined by puts the following pieces beneath the student event in this down light

parts.note: a rag is a British student charity carnival
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: head of points to the opening letter of the word college

explanation.surface: A calamitous student festival wrecked by a college principal.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAG is a British student fundraising carnival; in a down answer 'undermined by' means followed by.
explanation.definitionFit: Something catastrophic and dreadful in outcome is described as tragic, a near synonym.

clue.text: Excessive fondness of Venice's bigwig entertaining volunteers

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so the ruler's title takes the volunteers inside

parts.note: the Doge was the elected ruler of the Venetian republic
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A Venetian grandee doting on the volunteers he hosts.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides senility, the word has an older sense of foolish infatuation, being overly besotted with someone.

clue.text: Phoned and spoke

definitions.meaning: called on the telephone, past participle of ring
a crosspiece of a ladder or chair

explanation.surface: Someone called and talked.
explanation.definitionFit: A past form of ring means telephoned; a ladder's step is another name for a spoke or rail.

clue.text: Attendant responsible for little display of anger crossing street

indicators.note: crossing says the two words stretch across either side of the street abbreviation

parts.note: mini means small
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: An attendant to blame for a small outburst while crossing the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A ministrant is one who serves or assists, especially at a religious service, so an attendant.

clue.text: Become strange, always offering greeting

parts.note: go can mean become, as in go mad
odd means strange
ay (or aye) is a poetic word for ever

explanation.surface: Someone turning eccentric yet forever saying hello.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheery salutation used when meeting someone, especially in Australian or old-fashioned British speech.

clue.text: Having both feet on the ground — as, say, after parachute jump?

definitions.text: Having both feet on the ground

definitions.meaning: a parachutist drops from the sky to land

explanation.surface: Someone sensible, like a skydiver who has landed safely.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means realistic and unpretentious; literally a parachutist ends up descended onto the land.

clue.text: Italian in pain having a rest?

indicators.note: in places the Italian abbreviation within the word for pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: An Italian in agony, wondering if a break might help.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the weight off one's feet in a seat is a way of resting, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Hostile little bugs in destructive action? A farmer grew unhappy

definitions.text: Hostile little bugs in destructive action?

indicators.note: unhappy says the letters of these three words are disturbed into another order

explanation.surface: A farmer frets over pests destroying the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Biological warfare uses microbes as weapons, so tiny hostile organisms deployed to destroy.

clue.text: Putting right a part of the Army that's withering?

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
dying means withering away

explanation.surface: Repairing a branch of the army that is wasting away.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army corps that maintains and repairs equipment, which suits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To remedy is to correct or cure, so this present participle means correcting a fault.

clue.text: Leo has this place with wild animal getting horrible disease

parts.note: a den is a wild beast's lair
Ebola is a deadly viral fever

explanation.surface: A lion's lair harbouring a beast with a terrible illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leo' looks like a lion or a man; it is the constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the second-brightest star in the constellation Leo, marking the lion's tail.

clue.text: Good person felt irritation as one post-operation?

parts.note: St (saint) is the crossword stand-in for a good person
itched means felt an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: A patient, saintly sort, itching after surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: After surgery a wound is sewn up, so a patient recovering is sewn closed.

clue.text: Disposition to sow rage — be regretful losing head

parts.note: temper means a fit of anger

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter of the word for being regretful goes

parts.note: to lament is to express regret or grief

explanation.surface: A tendency to stir anger, then be sorry for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops L from LAMENT to give AMENT; 'to sow' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: One's natural character or mood is one's temperament, a direct synonym for disposition.

clue.text: Woman given command in Salvation Army

indicators.note: in places the word for order within the Salvation Army abbreviation

parts.note: to tell someone to do something is to order them

explanation.surface: A woman put in charge within the Salvation Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella is a girl's given name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Projecting beam or stake buried under rocky territory

indicators.note: buried under puts the wager below the territory in this down light

parts.note: Gib is short for Gibraltar, the British territory known as the Rock
a bet is a stake or wager

explanation.surface: A beam or post driven into rocky ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'buried under' means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallows is an upright post with an arm jutting out from which bodies were hung.

clue.text: Description of a Charlie in inferior part

definitions.meaning: a ... Charlie was the rear gunner of a bomber, or whoever brings up the rear
the last or lowest portion of something

explanation.surface: Charlie described as playing a minor role.
explanation.walkthrough: Tail-end Charlie is British slang, from RAF use, for the last person in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear or fag end of anything is its least significant portion, the lowest part.

clue.text: Nut to satisfy the boy at 23, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the words are heard when spoken, not seen as spelt

parts.note: to fill is to satisfy, as with a hunger; the boy named in the wordplay of 23 Across is Bert

explanation.surface: A nut that will feed a boy mentioned elsewhere in the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazelnut, especially the cultivated kind, goes by this name, so it is a type of nut.

clue.text: Goddess elevated in prayer festival

indicators.note: elevated says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A goddess raised up in worship at a religious celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals letters concealed in 'prayer festival'; 'elevated' turns them upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse deity of love and fertility, so an example of a divine female.

clue.text: Dissolute types given punishment at school, one boy included

indicators.note: included says the number and the name go inside the school punishment

parts.note: lines are sentences a pupil must copy out as punishment
I is the Roman numeral for one
Bert is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Debauched pupils given lines, one lad among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakes and debauchees who ignore moral restraint are exactly such loose-living people.

clue.text: Leave with quiet expression of surprise

parts.note: to go is to leave
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Departing with a hushed exclamation of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild exclamation, a polite substitute for God, voiced in amazement.

clue.text: Fool around, trying to be like Billy?

definitions.meaning: behave in a silly, playful way
a billy is a male goat, so one imitating it plays the animal

explanation.surface: Messing about, trying to imitate someone called Billy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to clown about; literally it is performing the role of a billy goat.

clue.text: Money haphazard — order lost

indicators.note: lost says the honour's letters go missing from the word for haphazard

parts.note: random means haphazard
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Cash kept in a jumble, its arrangement gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The rand is the currency of South Africa, so a specific unit of money.
